newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russia shows interest in Bulgarian privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Russia shows interest in Bulgarian privatisations.

text.p: Russia has shown interest in big Bulgarian privatisation deals including the sale of a stake in Neftochim oil refinery and of forklift truck producer Balkancar Holding, the head of the privatisation agency said on Monday.

"Russian investors have shown interest in participating in the privatisation of big firms in Bulgaria, such as Neftochim and Balkancar Holding," Veselin Blagoev said after talks with a Russian delegation headed by Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov, which arrived on Monday.
Blagoev said that Russia had shown special interest in tourism projects, most of them related to Black Sea resorts.

The meeting between the Bulgarian and Russian delegations will prepare issues for the agenda of an inter-governmental committee planned for June, Bulgaria's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
Bozhkov added the two sides had found a formula for the liberalisation of bilateral trade, which would be a step towards establishment of a free trade zone.

"We agreed a scheme used by Russia for signing an agreement for mutual liberalisation of trade with Poland and Slovakia through preparing a list of priority goods, which can be enlarged later," Bozhkov said.
Bozhkov said Russia had not made any payments on its $100 million debt to Bulgaria only because of "technical misunderstanding" between Bulgaria's state Bulbank and Russia's Vnesheconombank.
"The two sides are interested in solving the problem and I think that with the help of the two governments we will find a fast decision on the issue," Bozhkov said.

Trade ministry officials said Bulgaria and Russia had agreed last year that Moscow would supply equipment for Bulgaria's biggest metal works Kremikovtsi and military equipment against its $100 million debt. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
